modules.name: Cone registry, origins and versioning
modules.design_question: Which protected views apply at a location, where exactly are each origin, its elevation and field of view, and which version of each cone is this?
modules.method: Load the City ViewCone layer (EPSG:26910, 24 polygons) and cross-check the open-data GeoJSON (NAD83 geographic; GRS80 UTM conversion matches the service to 0.01 m). Store rings, not triangles: 23 have three vertices, cone 28 has five. Vertex 0 is the origin; sibling cones share it exactly (3.2.1/3.2.3/3.2.4, 9.1/9.2, B1/B2, G1/G2, J1/J2, 27.1/27.2; 3.2.2 differs 0.33 m), giving 16 origins as the City page lists. The two extreme rays are the vertical boundaries; the far edge is only a clip, except K, whose subject (City Hall) lies at the far edge. Version each cone by geometry hash, service edit dates and governing Council report; EFFECTIVE_DATE is informational (only view 28 differs from 2024-07-10). Audit landmark bearings: a boundary defined by a parcel corner must equal the bearing from the apex to that corner (H, J2, 28 and 9.1 west agree within 0.05 degrees; Trout Lake wedges equal the pre-2026 corners). Test points in projected metres with a 1.5 m on-edge band. Downtown and CBD subsets must use City boundary polygons digitised with provenance; the boxes listed are test boxes only.

City parcel polygons (S34) for corner audits

Downtown test box (lon -123.145 to -123.095, lat 49.268 to 49.2995), computed: all cones except 21, 27.1, 27.2 and 28 touch it.
Not-modelled table: C-3A City Hall views (about 9, words and images, no geodetic data), East Fraser Lands Mt Baker view, CD-1 (141) corridor, view 12.2 (no polygon).

modules.name: Lower-boundary parameter harvest and calibration
modules.design_question: What lower-boundary slope, or reference elevation and location, applies to each in-force cone when the City publishes no height surface?
modules.method: Each cone has origin O, elevation Lv and a lower boundary through a reference (Lr, Xr, Yr); k = (Lr - Lv)/Dr, with Dr measured by the same distance rule used later (store radial and axial k). Classify cones by definition text. S1, in-force reference: 28, H, J2 (printed coordinates); 27.1 and 27.2 (59.8 m and 54.3 m from the NE corner of 1975 E 12th Ave, located from the parcel layer, because the 2026 Trout Lake changes were referred back). S2, fitted to current-version City sheets: A, 3.2.3 (3.2.4 equals 3.2.3). S3, roof-aligned: E, G1, G2, J1, 9.1, 9.2, 20, 22; take Lr from City LiDAR 2022 building returns (highest roof point, rule documented) and test the method on A (1008 Cambie roof). S4, no definition text found: B1, B2, D, K, 10, 21, 3.2.1, 3.2.2. For S3 and S4 request free City View Cone Assessments: two points at least 1 km apart and two off-axis points per cone; fit slope and intercept together. Hold out one City point per cone. Flag queries outside the calibrated distance range. Record cone version, provenance and status for every number; computed values are labelled estimate, never City.

modules.name: Maximum-height surface engine
modules.design_question: What is the highest permitted geodetic elevation at every location, and which cone governs?
modules.method: Per cone, within its wedge, compute two candidate surfaces: radial Z_r = Lv + k_r*|p - O| and planar Z_a = Lv + k_a*((p - O) . u), u being the wedge bisector; k_r and k_a come from the same reference rule. The default limit is min(Z_r, Z_a) until an off-axis City sheet settles the rule: for Clinton Park the planar value is 1.0 m higher on axis at 1 km but 0.6 m lower at the wedge edge, so neither is always lower. Surface Z = min over cones in geodetic metres; no relaxation or aviation cap enters the minimum (M06 warns instead). Keep an argmin raster for governing cone and clause. Store parameters only (about 2 KB) and render on demand: a 2 m grid over the 4 km2 CBD is about 1 M cells in a Web Worker. Earth curvature is a switch, default planar; QE 3.2.3 values fit a line from Lv or a level sightline at Lv + 0.4 m with curvature (1.2 m at 3.9 km). Outside every polygon no view limit applies.
outputs: Limit raster (geodetic) for radial, planar and minimum rules, plus argmin cone ID raster.

modules.name: Vertical datum, frames and grade conversion
modules.design_question: How do geodetic cone heights relate to terrain, building base surface and the user's model so heights compare correctly?
modules.method: The PVG say geodetic without a datum (s.2, p.3). City LiDAR 2022 is CGVD28GVRD on the Metro Vancouver geoid (HTMVBC00, the renamed HTGVRDBC00) and BC legal surveys still use CGVD28 (LTSA CL 465C): treat cone heights as CGVD28 (assumption, flagged). Ground: City LiDAR 2022 bare earth (0.081 m, 95%); 1 km tiles, zipped LAS 16.45 MB to 2.74 GB each; fall back to the City 2013 DEM. LidarBC and HRDEM use CGVD2013: apply a user offset (about +0.15 m, preliminary 2013 figure) or a point value from NRCan GPS-H with CGG2013a and HT2.0 grids. Compare absolute elevations: City sheets give geodetic = base-surface elevation + height (1070 Barclay: 178.10 = 41.38 + 136.72). Horizontal frames: the service is labelled EPSG:26910 (NAD83 original), LiDAR is NAD83(CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD (about 0.1 m apart at Vancouver per Esri Canada); web basemaps may differ more (unverified). Check every origin Lv against LiDAR ground at the apex. Uploaded models: the user states the geodetic Z of one known point; store dZ.
outputs: terrain_cbd tiles (4 m, int16 cm), about 0.5 MB raw.
Datum offset table and georeference dialog values.

modules.name: Design-versus-cone checker and clause warnings
modules.design_question: Does an uploaded model or massing break a view cone, by how much, and which guideline clause applies?
modules.method: Convert uploads (Rhino 3dm via rhino3dm, OBJ, IFC via web-ifc) to the shared frame with the M04 transform. For each cone whose wedge meets the model footprint, clip meshes and roof faces to the wedge and compute penetration p = z - min(Z_r, Z_a) at the point nearest the origin (edges and faces), including appurtenances (clause 3.1.1, printed under heading 3.2, p.6). Report CLEAR, BOUNDARY (within 0.1 m) or INTERSECTS with depth, XYZ, governing cone and the distance rule that governed; mark points beyond the calibrated distance range as extrapolated. Cite clauses: 3.1.1; 3.1.2-3.1.4 minor encroachments (pp.6-7); 3.1.5 at most 2 m only if hardship is shown (p.7); 3.3 view shadows (p.7); 3.4 Exceptional Downtown Sites (p.7) through the user-enabled mask from M06. Never auto-classify minor elements, hardship or view shadows; show them as human-judgement notes. Every result carries the standing banner: estimate, not a City determination; PVG Table 1 cones only; the City View Cone Assessment governs.
outputs: Per-cone result: status, depth, XYZ, cone ID, rule.

modules.name: Relaxations, zoning and aviation obligations
modules.design_question: Which relaxations may apply by clause, and which zoning limits and federal aviation obligations apply to a downtown tower?
modules.method: Relaxations are not caps. The Higher Buildings Policy (31 Mar 2026) lets selected buildings enter QE view 3 and other Council-approved corridors; its heights (about 550-700 ft in the CBD, gateways about 400-515 ft) are guidance. Exceptional Downtown Sites (PVG 3.4; at least 8,000 m2) may also enter B1, B2, D and 12.2 and must keep views to the Lions (3.4.3); they get no relief from A, E, 9.x, J1, G or H. Implement a per-cone eligibility mask the user switches on, with clause and reason; never apply it automatically; draw guidance heights as reference lines. Zoning caps are typed from by-laws; zoning governs where lower. Aviation is rule-based: CAR 601.23(1) makes a structure an obstacle above 150 m AGL anywhere, or above 90 m AGL within 6 km of the geographical centre of an aerodrome (the CYHC water aerodrome and CBC7 heliport lie within about 2 km of the CBD); 601.24(1) requires notice to the Minister (form 26-0427, AC 601-007) and 601.24(2) marking and lighting per Standard 621. AC 601-007 notification surfaces: 60 m AGL basic; heliport 4% slope to 1,500 m. YVR zoning covers Richmond only. NAV CANADA outcomes (Holborn) are user-entered caps.
outputs: relaxation_masks.json: per cone, eligible instrument, clause, reason; user toggle default off.
aviation_rules.json: thresholds, positions and citations driving automatic warnings.

modules.name: Validation harness against City height sheets
modules.design_question: How do we prove the estimated surface matches the City's own numbers, separate fit from prediction, and keep proving it as the City amends views?
modules.method: Two suites. Gating: current-version City values (cone A 4 points and 3.2.3 5 points from the 3 Oct 2024 sheet, plus in-force definitions). Historical, never gating: the 9.2 points (pre-Feb 2026 origin), 1070 Barclay 3.2.1 and repealed 12.1.1 (2019), 2004 formula rows, 1133 W Georgia (2005, about 100.58 m, plus or minus 2 m band) and superseded Council values. Every value carries cone, origin, boundary definition, report and date. Report fit residuals and hold-out errors separately; never present fit residuals as accuracy. The build fails when a gating residual exceeds 0.1 m. Monthly job: poll the ViewCone layer lastEditDate (2026-05-05), dataLastEditDate (2026-04-15) and open-data modified date (2026-10-19), diff geometry hashes, and ignore EFFECTIVE_DATE. Request about 20 City assessments: near and far pairs at least 1 km apart, two off-axis points per cone, and one held-out point per cone. Transcribe numbers and coordinates only, with no names or page images.

modules.name: Viewpoint camera and lower-boundary overlay
modules.design_question: How should a design be viewed from each protected origin with the cone boundaries drawn as the City draws them?
modules.method: Place the camera at the origin (X, Y) at height Lv. Evidence suggests Lv is already eye level (1.4-3.5 m above 2002 contour ground at eight origins), so add 0 m by default and expose eye height as a user parameter. Aim along the cone bisector; set the field of view from the two boundary bearings plus a margin; draw vertical boundaries at the two bearings. City overlays show the lower boundary as a straight horizontal line in a photograph: in a rectilinear photograph that is a plane (planar model), in a cylindrical panorama a radial cone. Render both candidates and compare with the City 2026 reference photos (Cambie 9.x) before choosing. Rooftop viewpoints use the same camera class. Use City photos only as links, not copies.
outputs: Camera presets per view with FOV and bearings.
Overlay of boundaries on rendered view, radial and planar variants.

flags.claim: A cone's lower boundary is a flat plane at one constant geodetic height.
flags.correction: It is a rising sight line: Z = Lv + k*D.
flags.detail: PVG 'horizontal lower boundary' means horizontal in the view. City 2004 formula and current sheet points fit one k per cone: A 0.0589, 3.2.3 0.0004; the 9.2 value is now historical.

flags.claim: Vista README: origins can only be estimated from polygon geometry.
flags.correction: The polygon apex is the City's origin coordinate; sibling cones share it exactly and the City layer adds Lv.
flags.detail: 24 polygons give 16 apexes, matching the City's 16 origin points. Survey accuracy of the apex is unstated; 9.x apex are whole metres.

flags.claim: Cone heights are published nowhere, so no height test is possible.
flags.correction: No surface is published, but reference parameters appear in Council reports for several cones and the City issues per-site geodetic sheets.
flags.detail: In force now: 28, H, J2 printed; 27.1 and 27.2 parcel-located; A and 3.2.3 fitted; 3.2.4 equals 3.2.3. Service REFERENCE_* fields are empty for all 24.

flags.claim: YVR or harbour obstacle surfaces cap downtown heights.
flags.correction: YVR zoning (SOR/80-902) covers Richmond lands only; no zoning found for the harbour aerodrome or heliport.
flags.detail: Correct for zoning surfaces, but CAR 601.23 and AC 601-007 still apply to towers; NAV CANADA decisions are not public (Holborn, July 2026: about 27 m cut).

flags.claim: City sheet points all lie within 4 degrees of cone axes, so radial and axial distance cannot be separated.
flags.correction: 9.2 points lie 6.0-6.3 degrees off the bisector (A 0.5-1.9, 3.2.3 3.1-3.7). Planar fits better: A 0.012 vs 0.037 m, 9.2 0.008 vs 0.024 m.
flags.detail: Separation is modest (about 3x, under 0.05 m) and 9.2 is historical. Default to the lower of both rules until an off-axis City sheet or City confirmation.

flags.claim: 9.2 is calibrated (k 0.0488) for the current cone.
flags.correction: The sheet predates the Feb 2026 origin move; k belongs to the Walking Figures origin and is historical.
flags.detail: RTS 18292 App A pp.12-13 moves 9.1 and 9.2 to the City Hall campus stairs; the service apex and VIEWPOINT_LOCATION show the new origin. 9.2 removed from the calibrated count.

flags.claim: 20 published points currently fit within 0.07 m.
flags.correction: 9 current points on 2 cones (A 4, 3.2.3 5), in-sample; 3 points (9.2) are stale; the 8 Barclay values are not fitted.
flags.detail: Fit residual is not validation. Leave-one-out: A 0.017 m planar, 3.2.3 0.004 m; none tests extrapolation beyond 48 m.

flags.claim: The Higher Buildings Policy supplies height caps to include in the minimum surface.
flags.correction: It is a relaxation: Higher Buildings may enter QE view 3 and named corridors; heights are approximate guidance. PVG 3.4.2 lets Exceptional Downtown Sites also enter B1, B2, D, 12.2.
flags.detail: Modelled as user-enabled per-cone masks with clause and reason; never part of the minimum.

flags.claim: Trout Lake 27.1 and 27.2 have published lower-boundary parameters (59.8 m and 54.3 m at 495340.12, 5456431.39).
flags.correction: 59.8 and 54.3 m are in force, measured from the 1975 E 12th NE corner (parcel vertex 495332.94, 5456355.10). The printed coordinates belong to proposed 27.2 at 2670 Victoria Dr (68.9 m, not adopted).
flags.detail: Printed text sits in the Proposed column (x=322). k becomes 27.1 0.04533 and 27.2 0.03685. The critique's 'adopted 68.9 m, no coordinates' is also wrong.

flags.claim: Service polygons already hold 2026 Trout Lake boundaries and Council adopted them on 4 Feb 2026.
flags.correction: Council referred the Trout Lake amendments back (RTS 19750 p.4); service 27.1/27.2 equal the pre-2026 corner bearings.
flags.detail: Review continues; City page still shows 2024 images. PVG Table 1 still prints 'Amended 2026' for 27.x.

flags.claim: The far edge of each cone is a clip near Burrard Inlet, and all 24 cones are triangles.
flags.correction: Cone 28 has five vertices; K looks south to City Hall and its far edge is the subject boundary.
flags.detail: Store rings; take the two extreme rays as vertical boundaries.

flags.claim: No aviation rule applies downtown; it is case-by-case only.
flags.correction: No zoning surface, but CAR 601.23 makes any structure above 150 m AGL an obstacle (above 90 m within 6 km of an aerodrome); 601.24 requires notice and Standard 621 marking.
flags.detail: Competition towers are 244-305 m; CYHC and CBC7 lie within about 2 km of the CBD; AC 601-007 notification starts at 60 m AGL.

flags.claim: EFFECTIVE_DATE identifies the cone version.
flags.correction: Only view 28 shows 2026-02-04; 9.1, 9.2, H, J2 and 3.2.4 changed in 2025-26 yet show 2024-07-10.
flags.detail: Version by geometry hash, layer edit dates (2026-05-05, 2026-04-15) and Council report.

flags.claim: The 9.2 'roof of 485 W 8th Ave' test shows that roof alignments cannot give Lr.
flags.correction: The test paired the new apex with old-origin data and ignored a 15 m ground fall to 8th Ave; implied roof 43 m ASL is about 27 m above ground.
flags.detail: Roof route restored using LiDAR 2022 roofs; check the roof rule on A (1008 Cambie, implied 84 m ASL).

flags.claim: Radial distance is always the less conservative choice.
flags.correction: It depends on the reference bearing: Clinton Park planar is 1.0 m higher on axis at 1 km but 0.6 m lower at the edge; 27.2 planar is 4.3 m higher on axis at 1 km.
flags.detail: Use the lower of radial and planar. The axis could be the bisector, the bearing to the reference, or perpendicular to the boundary; only an off-axis City sheet settles it.

flags.claim: QE 3.2.3 fits a near-level plane at Lv plus eye height.
flags.correction: Slope is 0.00045 +/- 0.00008 (about 5 sigma from zero), so not level; a level sightline at Lv + 0.4 m with Earth curvature fits equally.
flags.detail: Curvature is 1.2 m at 3.9 km. A City point near 5.8 km would separate the two (about 0.6 m).

flags.claim: Eye height used at origins.
flags.correction: Not published. Lv exceeds 2002 contour ground by 1.4-3.5 m at A, B1, D, J1, 20, 21, 27, 28 (about 0 at 9.x), suggesting Lv is eye level.
flags.detail: Free-intercept fits give intercept = Lv + 0.3 m (A) and Lv - 0.2 m (3.2.3), excluding an extra 1.6 m. Camera default adds 0 m.

flags.claim: Slope distance D is radial from the origin.
flags.correction: Radial is the 2004 formula wording; a planar (axial) boundary is the City overlay geometry and fits the sheet better.
flags.detail: Default is min of both. Clinton Park, J2 and 27.2 references lie 8-26 degrees off axis, so the choice moves heights by metres.

flags.claim: A single smooth surface per cone.
flags.correction: 3.2.1 gives 123.201 m at one Barclay point but about 143.3 m at the rest.
flags.detail: Old sub-sections or stepped lower boundaries may exist (2011 report splits views into sub-cones). RTS 16338 App B shows 3.2.1 geometry unamended in 2024.

flags.claim: Named 'roof level' alignments give Lr directly.
flags.correction: Plausible via LiDAR 2022 roofs; the roof rule (parapet, penthouse, uppermost roof) is untested.
flags.detail: Check on A: 1008 Cambie roof implied 84 m ASL (D 1.35 km). 9.2: 485 W 8th implied 43 m ASL (D 256 m).

flags.claim: View 12.2 (Granville Bridge) still exists.
flags.correction: RTS 16338 Rec D (10 Jul 2024) orders a review of 12.2 and its draft Table 1 kept it; the Feb 2026 Table 1, open data, City layer and page have no 12.x view.
